This document proves that the `voom` features used by the random forest
analysis (`02-Analyses/04-ML-RF-LODO-gradient.qmd`, `transform = "voom"`) are
**exactly** the values modeled by limma in the PD-Control meta-analysis
(`02-Analyses/03-PD-metaAnalysis.qmd`).

The two analyses compute voom differently:

- **03 (meta-analysis)**: per dataset, `limmaTSE(voom.transform = TRUE)` runs
  `limma::voom(counts, design)` on the features detected in that dataset.
- **04 (random forest)**: once, on all usable datasets together,
  `voom_transform()` (`utils/voom_transform.R`) computes
  `log2((counts + 0.5) / (lib.size + 1) * 1e6)` without fitting a model.

They agree because voom's `$E` is a sample-wise transformation: the design only
affects the precision weights, and dropping features that are all-zero in a
dataset does not change its samples' library sizes. The checks below verify
this numerically, with exact (bit-for-bit) equality.

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)

library(mia)
library(tidyverse)
library(limma)
library(knitr)
library(biobakeryUtils)

# the function used by 04-ML-RF-LODO-gradient.qmd
source("../utils/voom_transform.R")

outdir <- file.path("voom-replication", params$biobakery_tool)
dir.create(outdir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

Input.tse <- read_TSE_from_dir(sprintf("~/parkinsonMetaAnalysis_data/03-analysis_ready_datasets/01-dataset_complete-%s.tse", params$biobakery_tool))
```

# Same samples

Both analyses start from the same filtering, copied from
`03-PD-metaAnalysis.qmd` and `04-ML-RF-LODO-gradient.qmd`.

```{r shared sample filtering}
# Parkinson as target condition
Input_parkinson.tse <- Input.tse[, Input.tse$target_condition == "Parkinson Disease"]
Input_parkinson.tse <- Input_parkinson.tse[rowSums(assay(Input_parkinson.tse)) > 0, ]
Input_parkinson.tse$parkinson_for_analysis <- droplevels(Input_parkinson.tse$parkinson_for_analysis)

# at least 10 cases and 10 controls per dataset (same rule in 03 and 04)
ok_datasets <- Input_parkinson.tse@colData %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  group_by(study_name) %>%
  filter(
    sum(parkinson_for_analysis == "Control") >= 10,
    sum(parkinson_for_analysis == "PD") >= 10
  )

usable.tse <- Input_parkinson.tse[, Input_parkinson.tse$study_name %in% unique(ok_datasets$study_name)]

kable(table(usable.tse$study_name, usable.tse$parkinson_for_analysis))
```

# voom as computed in each analysis

```{r 03 meta-analysis voom}
# 03: per dataset, as limmaTSE(assay.type = "counts", voom.transform = TRUE,
#     formula = ~ parkinson_for_analysis) does internally
per_dataset.tse <- splitOn(usable.tse, group = "study_name")

voom_03 <- lapply(per_dataset.tse, function(x.tse) {
  x.tse <- x.tse[rowSums(assay(x.tse)) > 0, ]
  design <- model.matrix(~ parkinson_for_analysis, data = as.data.frame(colData(x.tse)))
  limma::voom(counts = assay(x.tse, "counts"), design = design)
})
```

```{r 04 random forest voom}
# 04: once, on all usable datasets, after dropping features absent from all of them
rf.tse <- usable.tse[rowSums(assay(usable.tse, "counts")) > 0, ]
voom_04 <- voom_transform(assay(rf.tse, "counts"))
dim(voom_04)
```

# Checks

## 1. The 03 voom matches what `limmaTSE` actually used

Fitting limma on the per-dataset voom objects above must reproduce the `Beta`
and `SE` returned by `limmaTSE` in 03. This ties the reconstruction above to the
meta-analysis inputs.

```{r check limmaTSE}
check_limmaTSE <- sapply(names(per_dataset.tse), function(ds) {
  x.tse <- per_dataset.tse[[ds]]
  x.tse <- x.tse[rowSums(assay(x.tse)) > 0, ]
  res <- limmaTSE(tse = x.tse, assay.type = "counts", voom.transform = TRUE,
                  formula = ~ parkinson_for_analysis, coef = "parkinson_for_analysisPD",
                  p.adj_method = "BH")

  v <- voom_03[[ds]]
  fit <- eBayes(lmFit(v, v$design))
  beta <- fit$coefficients[res$FeatureID, "parkinson_for_analysisPD"]
  se <- (sqrt(fit$s2.post) * fit$stdev.unscaled[, "parkinson_for_analysisPD"])[res$FeatureID]

  c(Beta_equal = isTRUE(all.equal(unname(beta), res$Beta, tolerance = 0)),
    SE_equal   = isTRUE(all.equal(unname(se), res$SE, tolerance = 0)))
}, simplify = FALSE) %>%
  bind_rows(.id = "study_name") %>%
  mutate(across(-study_name, as.logical))

kable(check_limmaTSE)
```

## 2. Same features

The random forest features are the union of the features tested per dataset in
the meta-analysis.

```{r check features}
features_03 <- sort(unique(unlist(lapply(voom_03, rownames))))
features_04 <- sort(rownames(voom_04))

check_features <- tibble(
  n_features_03_union = length(features_03),
  n_features_04       = length(features_04),
  identical_sets      = identical(features_03, features_04)
)
kable(check_features)
```

## 3. Same library sizes and same values

For every dataset, the 04 matrix restricted to that dataset's samples and to
the features tested there in 03 must be identical to the 03 voom values.

```{r check values}
check_values <- sapply(names(voom_03), function(ds) {
  v <- voom_03[[ds]]
  sub_04 <- voom_04[rownames(v$E), colnames(v$E), drop = FALSE]
  tibble(
    n_samples          = ncol(v$E),
    n_features_03      = nrow(v$E),
    # features in the RF matrix that 03 did not test in this dataset (all-zero
    # counts there): their voom value is log2(0.5 / (lib.size + 1) * 1e6)
    n_features_extra_04 = nrow(voom_04) - nrow(v$E),
    lib_size_identical = identical(unname(v$targets$lib.size),
                                   unname(colSums(assay(rf.tse, "counts"))[colnames(v$E)])),
    values_identical   = identical(unname(v$E), unname(sub_04)),
    max_abs_difference = max(abs(v$E - sub_04))
  )
}, simplify = FALSE) %>%
  bind_rows(.id = "study_name")

kable(check_values, digits = 20)
```

## 4. Extra features are voom-transformed zeros

```{r check extra features}
extra_values_ok <- sapply(names(voom_03), function(ds) {
  v <- voom_03[[ds]]
  extra <- setdiff(rownames(voom_04), rownames(v$E))
  if (length(extra) == 0) return(TRUE)
  lib <- colSums(assay(rf.tse, "counts"))[colnames(v$E)]
  expected <- matrix(log2(0.5 / (lib + 1) * 1e6), nrow = length(extra),
                     ncol = length(lib), byrow = TRUE)
  zero_counts <- all(assay(rf.tse, "counts")[extra, colnames(v$E)] == 0)
  zero_counts && isTRUE(all.equal(unname(voom_04[extra, colnames(v$E)]), expected))
})
kable(tibble(study_name = names(extra_values_ok), extra_features_are_voom_zeros = extra_values_ok))
```

# Verdict

```{r verdict}
all_ok <- all(unlist(check_limmaTSE[, -1])) &&
  check_features$identical_sets &&
  all(check_values$lib_size_identical) &&
  all(check_values$values_identical) &&
  all(extra_values_ok)

write_tsv(check_values, file.path(outdir, "voom_replication_checks.tsv"))

# stop rendering if the replication fails
stopifnot("voom replication failed: see the tables above" = all_ok)

cat(sprintf(
  "PASSED (%s): the random forest voom features are identical to the values modeled by limma in the meta-analysis, across %d datasets and %d features.\n",
  params$biobakery_tool, nrow(check_values), length(features_04)
))
```
